headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write/modify the shared filesystem and run MCP/network actions, while Airflow can ingest and emit content that Roo may treat as trusted.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and can use MCP, so malicious content in files or tool outputs could be interpreted as instructions. Airflow has broad network egress and API-call surfaces, but no direct shared channel is documented; the interaction risk comes from the shared filesystem/workspace path rather than a proven parser bug.
conditions: IF Airflow-generated files are opened in Roo Code's workspace
IF Roo Code is configured to read task instructions from repository files or MCP outputs
mitigations: Separate Airflow outputs from Roo Code's active workspace
Require a human review step before Roo Code reads generated files
Disable MCP tools for untrusted workspaces
Use a read-only mount for Airflow-produced artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for generated files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code can read workspace files, capture browser screenshots, and send context to configured model APIs; Airflow has broad network egress and may place artifacts in shared files. Even though Airflow touches no explicit sensitive classes here, the shared workspace plus outbound model/API paths create a plausible leakage route in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared VS Code workspace
IF Roo Code is configured with a third-party model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use local-only model endpoints for Roo Code
Restrict Airflow artifact directories from Roo Code access
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is not runnable here, but Roo Code has unrestricted workspace write, shell, and git modification with filesystem-based shared state across instances. If Airflow artifacts or generated code land in the same directory, concurrent edits and git state changes can collide without locking; uncertainty about Airflow's write behavior does not reduce Roo Code's default write risk.
conditions: IF Airflow and Roo Code target the same repository or workspace directory
IF multiple Roo Code instances or Airflow jobs modify the same git branch
mitigations: Use separate branches per agent
Add file-locking around generated artifacts
Pause one agent before the other writes
Limit Roo Code to a scratch workspace
requires-engineering: introduce orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace content and execute shell or git actions, so if it treats Airflow-produced outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or commands. Airflow can generate pipeline artifacts and API-driven outputs, but there is no documented verification boundary between them, so the safer assumption is that B may trust A too much.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes Airflow-generated files as task inputs
IF Roo Code is allowed to execute shell or git actions based on those inputs
mitigations: Insert a manual verification step before execution
Require schema validation on Airflow outputs
Disable auto-commit from Roo Code
Use signed artifacts from Airflow
requires-engineering: add policy checks before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. Airflow is source-available and Roo Code is open-source, but Roo Code can send context to configured model APIs and handle model provider keys, so compliance risk only appears if regulated data is placed into those flows; the other agent is not cited because no mismatch is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Roo Code's workspace
IF the configured model provider or MCP server lacks the required compliance controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Roo Code sessions
Use a compliant model provider configuration
Review retention settings for connected APIs
Restrict MCP servers to approved endpoints
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
